name: Tomato
description: A fruit native to the Americas that has undergone centuries of cultivation and hybridization and is now grown and eaten around the world.

events.title: Tomatoes grew wild in the Andes
events.description: Tomatoes grew wild in the Andes of western South America before Europeans arrived in the Americas.

events.title: Tomatoes were cultivated and spread northward
events.description: Indigenous people cultivated tomatoes and eventually brought the plant northward through Central America and into Mexico.

events.title: Tomatoes were cultivated in Mexico
events.description: When the Spanish arrived in the early 16th century, they found inhabitants growing tomatoes as a food crop called "tomatl".

events.title: Tomatoes were introduced to Spain
events.description: Tomato seeds were brought from Mexico to Spain by early Spanish explorers.

events.title: Tomatoes spread to Italy
events.description: After reaching Spain, tomatoes spread to Italy and began to be incorporated into regional cuisine.

events.title: Tomatoes spread throughout Europe
events.description: Over the following decades, tomato plants were cultivated throughout Europe, primarily as ornamental plants.

events.title: Tomatoes were considered poisonous
events.description: Many Europeans mistakenly believed tomatoes were poisonous, contributing to names such as "poison apple."

events.title: Tomatoes returned to the Americas
events.description: Tomatoes were brought back to the Americas by European colonists.

events.title: Tomatoes were grown by Thomas Jefferson
events.description: Thomas Jefferson reportedly grew tomatoes in his vegetable garden at Monticello and enjoyed eating the fruit.

events.title: Tomatoes became widely popular in the United States
events.description: Tomato popularity became widespread throughout the United States.

events.title: Tomatoes were legally classified as vegetables
events.description: The U.S. Supreme Court case Nix v. Hedden resulted in tomatoes being considered vegetables for tariff purposes.
